item.title: Numbers and tensors
item.description:
Numeric types are simple (scalar) data types of TrustLang. The basics of typing are described on the page Type system, while arrays, ranges and (in perspective) tensors — in the section Ranges, arrays and tensors.

Integers

The names of integer types correspond to their bit width: :Int8, :Int16, :Int32, :Int64. An integer literal gets the minimum signed type into which its value fits (for example, 5 → :Int8), and a value that does not fit into :Int64 becomes :BigInteger. The type of a literal can be set by the explicit annotation literal :Type (for example, 1 :Bool, 255 :Int16) — when leaving the type range, a compilation error occurs, not a silent overflow.
